arxiv-1808-00976.title: Continuous Tensor Network States for Quantum Fields
arxiv-1808-00976.creator: Antoine Tilloy, J. Ignacio Cirac
arxiv-1808-00976.description: Abstract We introduce a new class of states for bosonic quantum fields which extend tensor network states to the continuum and generalize continuous matrix product states (cMPS) to spatial dimensions d ≥ 2 d\geq 2 . By construction, they are Euclidean invariant, and are genuine continuum limits of discrete tensor network states.

arxiv-2102-11183.title: Superradiance and anomalous hyperfine splitting in inhomogeneous ensembles
arxiv-2102-11183.creator: Petar Andrejić, Adriana Pálffy
arxiv-2102-11183.description: Abstract Collective effects in the interaction of light with ensembles of identical scatterers play an important role in many fields of physics. However, often the term “identical” is not accurate due to the presence of hyperfine fields which induce inhomogeneous transition shifts and splittings.

arxiv-2108-00293.title: Inverse Reinforcement Learning for Strategy Identification
arxiv-2108-00293.creator: Mark Rucker, Stephen Adams, Roy Hayes, Peter A. Beling
arxiv-2108-00293.description: Abstract In adversarial environments, one side could gain an advantage by identifying the opponent’s strategy. For example, in combat games, if an opponents strategy is identified as overly aggressive, one could lay a trap that exploits the opponent’s aggressive nature. However, an opponent’s strategy is not always apparent and may need to be estimated from observations of their actions.

arxiv-2108-10780.title: Unraveling correlated material properties with noisy quantum computers: Natural orbitalized variational quantum eigensolving of extended impurity models within a slave-boson approach
arxiv-2108-10780.creator: P. Besserve, T. Ayral
arxiv-2108-10780.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by P. Besserve, T. Ayral. We propose a method for computing space-resolved correlation properties of the two-dimensional Hubbard model within a quantum-classical embedding strategy that uses a Noisy, Intermediate Scale Quantum (NISQ) computer to solve the embedded model. While previous approaches were limited to purely local, one-impurity embedded models, requiring at most four qubits and relatively shallow circuits, we solve a two-impurity model requiring eight qubits with an advanced hybrid scheme on top of the Variational Quantum Eigensolver algorithm.

arxiv-2301-10884.title: Break It Down: Evidence for Structural Compositionality in Neural Networks
arxiv-2301-10884.creator: Michael A. Lepori, Thomas Serre, Ellie Pavlick
arxiv-2301-10884.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Michael A. Lepori, Thomas Serre, Ellie Pavlick. Though modern neural networks have achieved impressive performance in both vision and language tasks, we know little about the functions that they implement. One possibility is that neural networks implicitly break down complex tasks into subroutines, implement modular solutions to these subroutines, and compose them into an overall solution to a task — a property we term structural compositionality .

arxiv-2303-09857.title: Dual-path Adaptation from Image to Video Transformers
arxiv-2303-09857.creator: Jungin Park, Jiyoung Lee, Kwanghoon Sohn
arxiv-2303-09857.description: Abstract † † ∗ * Equal contributions. † \dagger Corresponding author. † † Official code: https://github.com/park-jungin/DualPath In this paper, we efficiently transfer the surpassing representation power of the vision foundation models, such as ViT and Swin, for video understanding with only a few trainable parameters.

arxiv-2304-10782.title: Contrastive Language, Action, and State Pre-training for Robot Learning Krishan Rana and Niko Sünderhauf are with the QUT Centre for Robotics, and Andrew Melnik is with the University of Bielefeld. We acknowledge continued support from the Queensland University of Technology (QUT) through the Centre
arxiv-2304-10782.creator: Krishan Rana*, Andrew Melnik and Niko Sünderhauf
arxiv-2304-10782.description: Abstract In this paper, we introduce a method for unifying language, action, and state information in a shared embedding space to facilitate a range of downstream tasks in robot learning. Our method, Contrastive Language, Action, and State Pre-training (CLASP), extends the CLIP formulation by incorporating distributional learning, capturing the inherent complexities and one-to-many relationships in behaviour-text alignment.

arxiv-2310-20113.title: Planets Across Space and Time (PAST) IV: The Occurrence and Architecture of Kepler Planetary Systems as a Function of Kinematic Age Revealed by the LAMOST-Gaia-Kepler Sample emcee ( Foreman-Mackey et al. 2013 ) , scikit-leart ( Pedregosa et al. 2012 ) , KeplerPORTs ( Burke & Catanzarite 2017 ) , num
arxiv-2310-20113.creator: Jia-Yi Yang, Di-Chang Chen, Ji-Wei Xie, Ji-Lin Zhou, Subo Dong, Zi Zhu, Zheng Zheng, Chao Liu, Weikai Zong, Ali Luo
arxiv-2310-20113.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Jia-Yi Yang, Di-Chang Chen, Ji-Wei Xie, Ji-Lin Zhou, Subo Dong, Zi Zhu, Zheng Zheng, Chao Liu, Weikai Zong, Ali Luo. One of the fundamental questions in astronomy is how planetary systems form and evolve. Measuring the planetary occurrence and architecture as a function of time directly addresses this question. In the fourth paper of the Planets Across Space and Time (PAST) series, we investigate the occurrence and architecture of Kepler planetary systems as a function of kinematic age by using the LAMOST-Gaia-Kepler sample.

arxiv-2312-15652.title: Generalization of Legendre functions applied to Rosen-Morse scattering states
arxiv-2312-15652.creator: F. L. Freitas
arxiv-2312-15652.description: Abstract A generalization of associated Legendre functions is proposed and used to describe the scattering states of the Rosen-Morse potential. The functions are then given explicit formulas in terms of the hypergeometric function, their asymptotic behavior is examined and shown to match the requirements for states in the regions of total and partial reflection.

arxiv-2401-03832.title: Covering one point process with another
arxiv-2401-03832.creator: Frankie Higgs, Mathew D. Penrose, Xiaochuan Yang
arxiv-2401-03832.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Frankie Higgs, Mathew D. Penrose, Xiaochuan Yang. Let X 1 , X 2 , … X_{1},X_{2},\ldots and Y 1 , Y 2 , … Y_{1},Y_{2},\ldots be i.i.d. random uniform points in a bounded domain A ⊂ ℝ 2 A\subset\mathbb{R}^{2} with smooth or polygonal boundary.

arxiv-2409-06817.title: Bifurcation Identification for Ultrasound-driven Robotic Cannulation
arxiv-2409-06817.creator: Cecilia G. Morales, Dhruv Srikanth, Jack H. Good, Keith A. Dufendach, Artur Dubrawski
arxiv-2409-06817.description: Abstract In trauma and critical care settings, rapid and precise intravascular access is key to patients’ survival. Our research aims at ensuring this access, even when skilled medical personnel are not readily available. Vessel bifurcations are anatomical landmarks that can guide the safe placement of catheters or needles during medical procedures.

arxiv-2412-08550.title: Sketch2Sound: Controllable Audio Generation via Time-Varying Signals and Sonic Imitations
arxiv-2412-08550.creator: Hugo Flores García io , Oriol Nieto i , Justin Salamon i , Bryan Pardo o , Prem Seetharaman i
arxiv-2412-08550.description: Abstract We present Sketch2Sound, a generative audio model capable of creating high-quality sounds from a set of interpretable time-varying control signals: loudness, brightness, and pitch, as well as text prompts. Sketch2Sound can synthesize arbitrary sounds from sonic imitations (i.e., a vocal imitation or a reference sound-shape).

arxiv-2503-08759.title: QUIET-SR: Quantum Image Enhancement Transformer for Single Image Super-Resolution
arxiv-2503-08759.creator: Siddhant Dutta, Nouhaila Innan, Khadijeh Najafi, Sadok Ben Yahia, Muhammad Shafique
arxiv-2503-08759.description: Abstract Recent advancements in Single-Image Super-Resolution (SISR) using deep learning have significantly improved image restoration quality. However, the high computational cost of processing high-resolution images due to the large number of parameters in classical models, along with the scalability challenges of quantum algorithms for image processing, remains a major obstacle.

pmc-10570407.title: Prediction of plasma volume and total hemoglobin mass with machine learning
pmc-10570407.creator: B Moreillon, B Krumm, J J Saugy, M Saugy, F Botrè, J M Vesin, R Faiss
pmc-10570407.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Hemoglobin concentration ([Hb]) is used for the clinical diagnosis of anemia, and in sports as a marker of blood doping. [Hb] is however subject to significant variations mainly due to shifts in plasma volume (PV). This study proposes a newly developed model able to accurately predict total hemoglobin mass (Hbmass) and PV from a single complete blood count (CBC) and anthropometric variables in healthy subject.

pmc-10661754.title: Anatomical characteristics of aortic valve diseases: Implications for transcatheter aortic valve replacement
pmc-10661754.creator: Yanren Peng, Xiaorong Shu, Yongqing Lin, Weibin Huang, Shuwan Xu, Jianming Zheng, Ruqiong Nie
pmc-10661754.description: BackgroundThe etiology of aortic stenosis (AS) significantly impacts transcatheter heart valve (THV) implantation, with rheumatic etiology posing challenges. The concept of valve anchoring during transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) for patients with aortic regurgitation (AR) remains unclear.ObjectiveThis study aims to investigate the clinical and CT anatomical characteristics of various aortic valve diseases.

pmc-11135889.title: Relationship between alveolar functional fraction and clinical outcomes in children during postoperative care after surgery for single-ventricular heart
pmc-11135889.creator: Dana Barry, Ellen A. Spurrier, Jigar C. Chauhan
pmc-11135889.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Background:Optimization of pulmonary to systemic blood flow (Qp: Qs) is the key to postoperative care of children with a single-ventricular heart. The ratio of end-tidal CO2 to partial pressure of CO2 called alveolar functional fraction (AFF) has shown a strong relationship with Qp: Qs in the catheterization lab in this population (with Qp: Qs of 1 correlating with AFF of 0.7).

pmc-11475345.title: Research on the Behavior Recognition of Beef Cattle Based on the Improved Lightweight CBR-YOLO Model Based on YOLOv8 in Multi-Scene Weather
pmc-11475345.creator: Ye Mu, Jinghuan Hu, Heyang Wang, Shijun Li, Hang Zhu, Lan Luo, Jinfan Wei, Lingyun Ni, Hongli Chao, Tianli Hu, Yu Sun, He Gong, Ying Guo
pmc-11475345.description: Simple SummaryCattle behavior recognition is an important field in animal husbandry. It can be used to understand the health status, emotions and needs of cattle. In this paper, an accurate and lightweight behavioral multi-detection model is proposed, which is adapted to real weather conditions.

pmc-11505006.title: Green Extraction of Bioactive Compounds from Apple Pomace from the Cider Industry
pmc-11505006.creator: Rosa Pando Bedriñana, Roberto Rodríguez Madrera, María Dolores Loureiro Rodríguez, Karelmar López-Benítez, Anna Picinelli Lobo, Alessandra Napolitano
pmc-11505006.description: The cider-making industry in Asturias generates between 9000 and 12,000 tons of apple pomace per year. This by-product, the remains of the apple pressing, and made up of peel, flesh, seeds and stems, is a valuable material, containing substantial amounts of antioxidant compounds associated with healthy properties.

pmc-11545796.title: Hair Growth Effect and the Mechanisms of Rosa rugosa Extract in DHT-Induced Alopecia Mice Model
pmc-11545796.creator: Ha-Rim Kim, Jung Up Park, Seung-Hyeon Lee, Jae Young Park, Wonwoo Lee, Kyung-Min Choi, Seon-Young Kim, Mi Hee Park, Cheng-Yang Huang
pmc-11545796.description: Rosa rugosa is a medicinal plant known for its potential anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, anti-cancer, and antimicrobial benefits. The pharmacological effects of Rosa rugosa extract on hair loss have not yet been documented. This research sought to assess the inhibitory effects and mechanisms of action of Rosa rugosa water extract (RWE) in a mouse model of dihydrotestosterone (DHT)-induced alopecia.

pmc-11590909.title: Voluntary Participation Mediates the Relationship Between Multi-Membership in Online Communities and Life Satisfaction Among Chinese Populations: A Gendered Perspective
pmc-11590909.creator: Xiaorui Huang, Mingqi Fu, Qinghua Yang
pmc-11590909.description: Whether and how multi-membership in online communities might relate to life satisfaction within the Chinese population remain unclear. This study adopts a gendered perspective to explore the mediating role of voluntary participation in the relationship mentioned above based on a cross-sectional analysis of 2558 respondents from the 2019 Chinese Social Survey (CSS).

pmc-11629676.title: Patients’ Preferences for the Treatment of a Single Missing Tooth in China: A Discrete Choice Experiment
pmc-11629676.creator: Ming-yu Zhao, Wen Zeng, Sze Ngai Chan, Jianhao Du, Naman Rao, Taoran Liu, Wai-kit Ming
pmc-11629676.description: PurposeThe main treatment options offered to patients to choose from when restoring a single missing tooth include tooth-supported three-unit fixed partial dentures (FPDs) and implant-supported single crowns (ISCs). However, due to the heterogeneity of current studies, it is difficult to objectively compare these two treatment strategies.

pmc-13233578.title: Neoadjuvant sintilimab plus chemotherapy in EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NEOTIDE/CTONG2104): phase II trial and correlative genomic analysis in China
pmc-13233578.creator: Chao Zhang, Ben-Yuan Jiang, Li-Xu Yan, Li-Shan Peng, Jin-Hu Li, Zhi-Yong Chen, Yu-Xuan Sun, Jian Su, Ri-Qiang Liao, Song Dong, Hong-Hong Yan, Chong-Rui Xu, Qing Zhou, Xue-Ning Yang, Zheng Hu, Yi-Long Wu, Wen-Zhao Zhong
pmc-13233578.description: SummaryBackgroundTo evaluate the efficacy and safety of neoadjuvant sintilimab, a programmed cell death 1 protein (PD-1) blockade combined with chemotherapy in patients with resectable stage II-IIIB epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).MethodsThis was a single-arm, open-label, phase II trial (CTONG2104) conducted in China.

pmc-13602695.title: Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR)-verified autoxidation and hydrolysis induce lipid degradation in pan-fried hand-grasp pancakes
pmc-13602695.creator: Pengyuan Wei, Jingjing Lun, Yihang Ding, Jinying Wang, Linshang Zhang, Cong Sun, Kaizhou Yang
pmc-13602695.description: This study investigated the effects of pan-frying on fat quality in hand-grasp pancakes. The results demonstrated that fats exhibited significant quality deterioration: acid value increased by 50%–85%, peroxide value rose by 175%–490%, and p-anisidine value elevated by 65%–430%. The increments of conjugated diene value and conjugated triene value ranged from 20% to 50% and 35% to 73%, respectively.
